configs.description: CRS326-24G-2S+RM - 24 10/100/1000 ports, two SFP+ cages and the RJ45 console. The box holds a 24 V 1.2 A adapter, rack ears and a screw set.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: The dimensions drawing has no rear view; the rear is read off studio photographs that look down on it, so the y positions are estimated.

The earthing stud has a wing nut (photograph 1941; the drawing's 11 mm). common/ground-stud draws a hex nut and a lug seat, so the stud is chassis art and exports no earth. The reason is the nearest the schema has: the part itself is what is missing, and the library has no `needs-part` reason.
gaps.wanted: A wing-nut earth stud part, so the stud is placed and not drawn as chassis art.

gaps.note: Searched the brochure, the quick guide page and the CSS326 quick guide for an LED table: none. The lamps carry the component's own vocabulary and no colour or meaning is stated.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's LED description for the CRS326.

gaps.note: Neither the brochure nor the product page gives a weight; the NetBox device type says 1.08 kg, a community figure not carried.
The saved product page carries no Discontinued badge and MikroTik publishes no end-of-life page, so no lifecycle is written.

gaps.wanted: an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.memory`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Powering is by the DC jack or by passive PoE on port 1, with a 24 V 1.2 A adapter in the box (brochure, Included); no power supply is built in, so none is drawn and there are no power bays. The product page gives the cooling type as passive. The round opening on the rear is a stamped fan-guard grille with four fan-mount holes and no fan fitted, so it is drawn as a vent and not a fan.

chassis.note: 443 wide, 44.5 high (the 1U pitch is 44.45), 144.6 deep. The side view dimensions 144.6 and the brochure and product page round it to 144 (443 x 144 x 44 mm); the drawing's figure is carried. The 11 mm the side view dimensions is the earthing stud's wing nut standing off the rear, not part of the depth. 443 is the body between the ear folds (the top plan shows no ears).

colour.note: median of the CSS326 straight-on photograph's body (#f5f5f5) and face (#dadada); the CRS326 is the same white and grey in its own photographs.

console.note: The RJ45 serial port (brochure: Serial port RJ45) is the shielded jack under the printed CONSOLE, at the left of the front. The CSS326 has none; its drawing keeps the same square blank.

datasheet.note: The CRS326-24G-2S+RM brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model (the product page's Brochure link): product code, CPU, 512 MB RAM, 16 MB flash, 98DX3236A1 switch chip, 24 10/100/1000 ports, two SFP+ cages, SwOS / RouterOS dual boot, 9 - 30 V input by jack or passive PoE, 443 x 144 x 44 mm, -40 to +60 C tested, 24 W maximum, serial RJ45; the features list and the included parts (24 V 1.2 A adapter, rack ears, screw set). The 24 W is unqualified, so it is filed as the maximum.

dc-in-rating.note: The rear prints "DC 10-28V" beside the jack (photograph 1941): the `input-voltage` of the dc-in jack, carried as printed. The brochure's Included list gives a 24 V 1.2 A adapter, the `current-max-a`. The brochure's 9 - 30 V and the product page's 10-30 V are in `attrs.power`. The CRS326 documents held give no barrel size (the CSS326 quick guide states one, not this model's document); the jack is the library's one nominal `dc-barrel`.

dc-input.note: The brochure lists the supported input voltage as 9 - 30 V (jack or passive PoE); the product page 10-30 V for both inputs; the rear prints DC 10-28V. The three disagree and none is the others' scope: the rear legend is drawn as printed and the brochure and page ranges are in attrs. The jack is the placed common/dc-barrel (`dc-in`), positioned on the bore of photograph 1941. The CRS quick guide is not held as text, so no barrel size is asserted for the CRS.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (brochure and product page, Included: Rack ears, Screw set). The drawing's side view shows the ear plate at the front end of the body, on the face, so the shipped position is flush and the ear is drawn at the face plane; the top plan shows no ears (443 is the body). The ears are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Three jack blocks, each a 59.9 x 25.5 plate at 36.7, 100.3 and 163.8 mm (63.5 mm step), four columns of two jacks on 13.97 mm pitch, first jack centre 46.1 mm; the upper row is 13.4 mm above the lower and the upper jacks' latch notch is up, the lower's down. The SFP+ cages are 15.7 mm wide at centres 238.5 and 260.2 mm (21.7 mm apart), top at 25.0 mm. The lamp band along the bottom starts at 35.4 mm. The CONSOLE jack position is the empty square the drawing keeps at the left, 15.2 x 11.5 mm; the 15.8 x 13.2 mm registry jack is centred in it, 1.7 mm taller than the drawn square, so its bottom edge (22.7 + 13.2 = 35.9) runs 0.5 mm into the lamp band, which starts at 35.4; the photograph shows the jack reaching the band the same way and the overlap is kept. Colours are medians of the straight-on CSS326 studio photograph (plate #dadada, jack plates #bebebe, lamp band #8f8f8e).

gate-1.note: The drawing's front view body is 1744 px across at 200 dpi for the printed 443 (3.937 px per mm) and 176 px down for 44.5 (3.955 px per mm), 0.5 percent apart, so it is orthographic and every x and y below is taken at 3.94 px per mm from the body's top-left corner. The jack pitch then reads 55 px = 13.97 mm, the registry's ganged RJ-45 pitch, on a quantity the scale never saw.

lamps.note: Each port has one lamp box, 3.2 mm square at 5.9 mm spacing, pair centre 0.6 mm left of the column centre (drawing, four pairs measured), centre 38.0 mm. PWR and USR are lamps at 17.2 and 32.8 mm. Each SFP+ has an ACT/LINK lamp under the cage centre and a 10G lamp 10.6 mm to its right, joined to the cage by a printed line. No document held says what a lamp shows (the brochure and the saved quick guide give no LED table), so none carries states beyond the component's own.

port-numbering.note: Printed numbers 1 to 24 in lamp boxes under the jacks, a pair under each column, left box first (1 2, 3 4 ... 23 24). Which jack takes which number is read from the POE IN bracket, which the drawing and the photograph both wrap round the lower left jack: port 1 is the passive PoE input (brochure: supported input voltage jack or passive PoE; quick guide: the first Ethernet port accepts passive PoE), so the lower jack of each column takes the odd number and the upper the even. No source prints a number on the jack itself. The pair's left lamp is taken as the odd port's and the right as the even port's; that pairing is estimated.

rear-layout.note: estimated - no rear elevation is held; the positions are read off the studio rear photograph 1941. It looks down on the rear, so x is taken at the photograph's 3.995 px per mm across the 443 mm body and y is estimated: the metalwork is the CSS326's, which the straight-on rear photograph 1268 shows with a 8 percent shorter vertical scale, and the shared items (blank plate, three vent fields, two round knock-outs, the round vent, three screws) take that photograph's figures, which agree with the CRS's in x to 1.5 mm. They are good to about 1.5 mm in x and 2 mm in y. The CRS's cable slot runs on to hold the DC jack, 58 mm long against the CSS's 31 mm, and the CRS prints DC 10-28V where the CSS prints DC 8 - 30V. The earthing stud has a wing nut (the drawing's 11 mm). It is drawn as chassis art at the stud's position from the photograph, because the library's common/ground-stud draws a hex nut and a lug seat the stud does not have; the gap `earth-stud-part` asks for a wing-nut stud part. The CRS prints an earth symbol above it; the CSS prints none. The DC jack is the placed common/dc-barrel (`dc-in`), its bore centred on the photograph's.

reset.note: RES is a round hole at 25.0 mm, centre 38.0 mm, between PWR and USR; the quick guide's reset section says to hold the button at boot until the lamp flashes. The library's recessed pinhole is used.

sources.note: Dimensions drawing "CRS/CSS326-24G-2S+ dimensions", MikroTik, printed 19.09.2023 (file CRS_CSS326-24G-2S_dimensions_230943.pdf, rendered at 200 dpi; the title block reads CRS/CSS326-24G-2S+ dimensions): front, side, top plan and isometric. The front view is the CSS326's (it prints Cloud Smart Switch and has no console jack) and is used for the shared metalwork. The port numbers are printed inside the lamp boxes on the metal; silkscreen is painted under a placed lamp, so they are drawn just under each lamp instead, 4.5 mm below its centre. CRS326-24G-2S+RM brochure, MikroTik (file CRS326-24G-2SRM_211044.pdf; no date is printed, the file name carries a revision stamp): specification table, features, included parts. CRS326-24G-2S+RM product page, MikroTik (saved 2026-10-26): dimensions, powering, cooling type, included parts (rack ears). The product-page studio photographs 1301 (front) and 1941 (rear), and the saved quick guide page for the G1 CRS series (no figures saved). The NetBox community device type and elevations were read as a second opinion only. No figure numbers: MikroTik prints none. The device name spells MikroTik's + as -plus because a directory name cannot carry +; model: keeps the + as printed, and every MikroTik device name in the library does the same.
